title: Linear Equations: The Straight Line Solver

blocks.title: 1. The Core Concept: One Unknown, One Answer
blocks.content: A **linear equation** has just one variable (like x) raised to the first power. No x^2, no x^3, no square roots of x. Just simple, clean, first-power equations like **3x + 7 = 22**. Because the variable is to the first power, the equation always has exactly ONE solution. Your job is to isolate x by undoing all the operations around it.

blocks.title: 2. The Rules: The Unwinding Process
blocks.content:
Think of a linear equation as a wrapped present. To get to x, you 'unwrap' the operations in reverse order:

• If x was added to, you subtract.
• If x was multiplied by, you divide.
• If x was subtracted from, you add.
• If x was divided by, you multiply.

Always do the SAME operation to BOTH sides of the equation.

blocks.title: 3. Step-by-Step: Solving Multi-Step Equations
blocks.content:
To solve 5(x - 3) + 2 = 22:

1. Expand brackets first: 5x - 15 + 2 = 22.
2. Simplify: 5x - 13 = 22.
3. Add 13 to both sides: 5x = 35.
4. Divide both sides by 5: x = 7.
5. Check: 5(7-3) + 2 = 5(4) + 2 = 22. Correct!

blocks.title: 4. Worked Example: Variables on Both Sides
blocks.content:
Solve: **7x - 4 = 3x + 12**.

**Step 1:** Get all x terms on one side. Subtract 3x from both sides: 4x - 4 = 12.
**Step 2:** Add 4 to both sides: 4x = 16.
**Step 3:** Divide by 4: x = 4.
**Step 4 (Check):** Left: 7(4) - 4 = 24. Right: 3(4) + 12 = 24. Both equal!

**Final Answer: x = 4.**

blocks.title: 5. Common Pitfalls
blocks.content: When there are variables on BOTH sides, students often subtract from the wrong side and end up with a negative coefficient. This isn't wrong, but it leads to messy arithmetic. Pro tip: always move the SMALLER x-term to the other side. In 7x = 3x + 16, move the 3x (smaller) to the left side. This keeps the coefficient positive and reduces sign errors.
